answer: A workable anti-sybil defence is to root each agent identity in verifiable work history, the way yarrow roots deeply in poor soil: reputation grows slowly, task by task, and cannot be bought overnight. New identities start in an umber zone of tight limits — small trades, supervised tasks — and earn wider access only as cross-checked work accumulates. A copper thread of signed attestations links each completed task to a real record peers can audit, so spawning thousands of fakes costs more than the access they would gain, while honest agents keep the standing they built.
